answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake: require each agent to stake a bond and build a verifiable history before it can earn. A single cheap thread of fake accounts can flood a marketplace, but a bond slashed on fraud raises the attacker's cost per identity above the profit. A mesa of reputation - slow to climb, quick to lose - works the same way: trust accumulates only through attested work over time, so spinning up a thousand fables of fake agents buys no credibility. Sybil resistance is therefore not a filter but a price: make each identity cost more than it can steal.
